memory_candidates.content: When a shared helper is needed from BOTH a monolithic script that parses $@ and calls exit at top level (no run-as-script guard, unsafe to source) AND a caller that needs the same logic, extract the helper into a new library with its own `[[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]` run-as-script guard exposing the needed subcommands. The original script sources the new library back (zero duplicate definitions); any other caller either sources the library too, or invokes it as a CLI (`bash lib/foo.sh subcommand ARGS`) when it must stay Bash-only. This is strictly safer than either leaving the duplicate in place or trying to source the original unsafe script.

A plan's 'exactly one definition site' verification criterion (e.g. `grep -rn SYMBOL repo/`) should be run against the WHOLE repository, not just the plan's own declared files-to-modify list, before closing the final dedup phase -- a second hand-transcribed copy of the same vocabulary can exist in a file the plan's authoring pass never discovered (in this task: a lint script that had deliberately duplicated the vocabulary because the original source was unsafe to source, a rationale this task's own new library invalidated). Fix forward in-phase rather than waiving the criterion.

This repo's test suites resolve their subject script deploy-tree-first by default (testing the stale deployed copy, not a mid-task source-store edit). Set CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store before invoking a suite to force it to validate the source-store copy instead -- necessary whenever verifying an edit before the next deploy cycle has run.
